title: Homeward bound
context: Return-journey operations, Earth photography, communications and trans-Earth coast. The trans-Earth injection burn is reported in this UTC day.
timeBasis: UTC calendar day; mission times are from the uncorrected transcript.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Burn complete. Residuals: plus three balls 40, plus four balls 7, plus four balls 2, DELTA-V counter 102.1. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Copy, Apollo 11. Looks good to us. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. How about coming up with a good communications attitude for us to go to between now and the time we maneuver at TEI attitude.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, sir. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11, Houston. A couple of things for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Mike, you can maneuver to your preliminary TEI attitude as shown on page 398 of the flight plan, and the high gain angles are good as shown in the flight plan, and we'd like you to dump the waste water at 131 05 down to 10 percent. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Understand. I'm going to go to roll 1.1, pitch zero - or 52.6, and yaw 13.8, and you want a waste water dump 10 percent starting at 131 05.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative. Right out the LOS.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Maneuver is in progress, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Copy, 11. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Apollo 11 under high gain. How do you read?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Five by, 11. How me? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You're loud and clear, Charlie. What - What numbers are you looking at for TEI TIG preliminary; 135 hours 23 minutes, something like that?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative, Mike. We're looking at about nominal time. We've considered kicking it up a REV, but we don't think this REV track is going to be any good since we had the RCS burn and we need some more tracking to get you a good TEI. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's what we're looking for.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Looks like it's going to be pretty relaxed time here for the next couple of hours. We'll have you a PAD, of course, the next REV or so, and we'll keep you posted on TEI. Looks like nominal time. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And your little maneuver back here a moment ago will put you about 20 miles ahead of the LM at TEI.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Imagine that place has cleared out a little bit after that rendezvous. You can find a place to sit down almost, huh?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Our MOCR's about empty right now. We're taking it a little easy. How does it feel up there to have some company?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Damn good, I'll tell you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: I'll bet. I bet, you'd almost be talking to yourself up there after 10 REVS or so.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: No, no. It's a happy home here. It'd be nice to have company. As a matter of fact, it'd be nice to have a couple of hundred million Americans up here.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Well, they were with you in spirit.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Let them see what they're getting for their money.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Well, they were with you in spirit anyway, at least that many. We heard on the news today, 11, that last night - yesterday after you made your landing, New York Times came out with a - headlines, the largest headlines they've ever used in the history of the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Save us a copy.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I'm glad to hear it was fit to print.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: It was great.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's why we didn't read you up any newscast. There really wasn't anything to talk about.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Hello, there, Boss.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We've got 10 minutes to LOS; see you over the hill at 131 48. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Charlie. I'll dump the water as soon as we go around the corner.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Everything's looking real good now.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. Same here.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Coming up about 4 30 LOS. You're looking great on all your systems. Eagle is purring right along after an hour 30 without any cooling. The PNGS is still looking good. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Will you verify that your rendezvous radar transponder is off? Over. (GODS NET 1) Tape 84/8 Page 497

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It's not, but I'll get it off.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We were seeing - believe it or not, we were seeing some funnies on the Eagle's rendezvous radar, and that was the only theory that we had. It looked like it was a good one.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Good theory.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We are standing by. Everything is looking great here. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Apollo 11. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. If you guys want it, we've got some news, here, we can read up. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Be pleased to have it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. Starting off: Congratulatory messages on the Apollo 11 mission have been pouring into the White House from world leaders in a steady stream all day. Among the latest are telegrams from Prime Minister Harold Wilson of Great Britain and the King of Belgium. The world's press has been dominated by news of Apollo 11. Some newsmen estimate that more than 60 percent of the news used in papers across the country today concerned your mission. The New York Times which, as we mentioned before, has had such a demand for its edition of the paper today (even though it ran 950 000 copies) said it will reprint the whole thing on Thursday as a souvenir edition. And Premier Alexei Kosygin has sent congratulations to you and President Nixon through former Vice President Humphrey who is visiting Russia. The cosmonauts have also issued a statement of congratulations. Humphrey quoted Kosygin as saying "I want you to tell the President and the American people that the Soviet Union desires to work with the United States in the cause of peace."

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And Mrs. Robert Goddard said today that her husband would have been so happy. "He wouldn't have shouted or anything. He would just have glowed." She added, "That was his dream, sending a rocket to the Moon." People around the world had many reasons to be happy about the Apollo 11 mission. The Italian police reported that Sunday night was the most crime free night of the year. And in London, a boy who had the faith to bet $5 with a bookie that a man would reach the Moon before 1970 collected $24.000. That's pretty good odds.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: You're probably interested in the comments your wives have made. Neil, Jan had said about yesterday's activities, "The evening was unbelievably perfect. It is an honor and a privilege to share with my husband, the crew, the Manned Spacecraft Center, the American public, and all mankind; the magnificent experience of the beginning of lunar exploration." She was then asked if she considered the Moon landing the greatest moment in her life. She said "No, that was the day we were married." And Mike, Pat said simply, "It was fantastically marvelous." Buzz, Joan said - apparently couldn't quite believe the EVA on the Moon. She said, "It was hard to think it was real until the men actually moved. After the Moon touchdown, I wept because I was so happy." But she added, "The best part of the mission will be the splashdown."

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: In other news, and there was a little bit, another explorer: Thor Heyerdahl had to give up his attempt to sail a papyrus boat across the Atlantic. The storm damaged boat was abandoned about 650 miles from Bermuda. The speed of the craft had been reduced to about 25 miles a day, and Heyerdahl said the object of the voyage had not been to provide an endurance test for the crew.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Looking at the world of sports, let's see here. While you were busy the other day, Joe Namath and football Commissioner Pete Rozelle made the announcement that "Broadway Joe" had agreed to sell his interest in the Bachelors III restaurant and report to the New York Jets. Joe arrived at the Jets' training camp today and had his first workout. Several other Jet players who had held out along with Joe also reported. And Davy Hill, from Jackson, Michigan, won his third major golf in as many starts in the past week. He won the Philadelphia Classic. Hill has won four tournaments so far this year and is the leading money winner this year with a cool $129.000. And in baseball, the west division of the National League remains a tight race. LA and San Francisco are one game behind league leading Atlanta. The Astros have a record of 48 wins and 48 losses, and are now in fifth place, seven games out. A twin bill between the Astros and Cincinnati last night was postponed because of rain. The Chicago Cubs are still in first place in the East Division. They lead the New York Mets by four and one half games. And in the American League, Baltimore is breezing toward the Eastern Division title. They lead second place Boston by 11 games. Looking ahead, the All Star baseball game is scheduled for tomorrow. And President Nixon was scheduled to see the game and then leave immediately after the game for the Pacific splashdown area before going on his tour of Europe. And that about covers the news this day. You guys have been making most of it and I'm sure we couldn't fill you in on any of the details that you don't already know. Out.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Thank you much, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We've got a preliminary TEI 30 PAD, if you're ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Coming at you. TEI 30, SPS/G&N: 36691; minus 061, plus 067 135 23 4149; NOUN 81, plus 32020, plus 06713, minus 02773 181 054 013; NOUN 44, HA is NA, plus 00230 32833 228, DELTA VC 32625 24 1510 355. Next three lines are NA. NOUN 61 plus 1103, minus - minus 17237 11806 36275 195 04 52. Your set stars are Deneb and Vega, 242 172 012. We like two jet ullage to 16 seconds. The horizon will be on the 11 degree mark at TIG minus 2 minutes. And other comments: your sextant star is visible after GET of 134 50. Ready for your readback. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. We have a TEI 30, SPS/G&N: 36691, minus 061, plus 067 135 23 4149; plus 32020, plus 06713, minus 02773 181 054 013; NA, plus 00230, plus 32833 228 32625, 24 1510 355; NA three times, plus 1103, minus 17237 11806 36275 195 04 52. Deneb and Vega 242 172 012, two jet ullage, 16 seconds; horizon 11 degree line at TIG minus 2 minutes; sextant star visible after 134 50. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Mike. Good readbaek. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Seven minutes to LOS; next AOS 133 46. You're looking good going over the hill. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We're standing by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'd like you, sometime at your convenience, to stir up the CRYO's on this pass. And we're wondering if you got the fuel cell purge. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. *** fuel cell purge ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again. You're breaking up.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. The O2 fuel cell purge is complete.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11, Houston. We've got a load for you, if you give us P00 and ACCEPT. The load consists of a CSM pre TEI state vector that's going in the CSM slot, and a post-TEI state vector that'll go into the LM slot, if that's okay; and also a TEI target load. Any comments? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: P00 and ACCEPT. You got it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, 11, Houston. A reminder: you can scratch the VERB 66 at 134 30.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Understand.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, 11, Houston. For your information, Eagle, we had an ISS fail light came on at about 3 19 due to a CDU overheating; and at about this time at AOS it looks like we're about to lose the platform. *** Three asterisks denote clipping of words and phrases.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We got the load in. You can have the computer - -

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: 11. Are you through with the computer?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative, Buzz.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: All right. That's timing for you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And, Apollo 11, Houston. Your friendly White Team has your coming home information, if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Apollo 11. Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. Got two PADS for you, TEI 30 and then a TEI 31. TEI 30 SPS/G&N: 36691, minus 061, plus 066 135 23 4156. NOUN 81: 32 - correction, plus 32011, plus 06818, minus 02650 181 054 014. Apogee is NA, perigee plus 00230 3286 - correction, 32836; burn time 2 28 32628 24 1511 357. Next three lines are NA. NOUN 61: plus 1103, minus 17237 11806 36275 195 04 52. Set stars are Deneb and Vega, 242 172 012. We'd like ullage from two jets for 16 seconds, and the horizon is on the 10 degree line at TIG minus 2 minutes; and your sextant star is visible after 134 plus 50. Stand by on your readback. I have a TEI 31 if you're ready to copy. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. TEI 30, SPS/G&N: 36691, minus 061, plus 066 135 23 4156, plus 32011, plus 06 818, minus 02650, 181 054 014; apogee NA, plus 00230 32836 228 32628 42 1511 357, NA three lines, plus 1103, minus 17237 11806 36275 195 04 52, Deneb and Vega, 242 172 012, two jet ullage, 16 seconds, horizon out of the window, 10 degrees, TIG minus 2 minutes, sextant star at 134 10. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. Good readback. You're very weak. If you're ready to copy, I got a TEI 31 for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You were cut out. Say again.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by one.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead. I'm ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. TEI 31, SPS/G&N: 36691, minus 061, plus 066 137 22 3985, plus 32838, plus 06845, minus 02487, NA, pitch 052. Rest of the PAD is NA. Ready for your readback. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. TEI 31, SPS/G&N: 36691 minus 061, plus 066, 137 22 3985, plus 32838, plus 06845, minus 02487, NA, pitch 052. The rest is NA. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Good readback. And, Buzz, did you say sextant star is visible after 134 50?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: No. I wrote down 134 10. I wasn't real sure about that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. It went by me there. RETRO caught it. It's 134 50. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. 134 50. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. After the burn, we'd like you to trim X and Z. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And that's to 0.2 foot per second, as shown in the flight plan.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Sounds like there's a story behind that one, too.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We'll tell you when you get back.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Would you verify that you've stirred up the CRYO's? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. We've stirred them up.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You are GO for TEI. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Apollo 11. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. You've got about 8 minutes till LOS. Your AOS with the burn, 135 34 05, no burn 135 44. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. One minute to LOS. Go sic 'em.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We'll do it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello Apollo 11. Houston. How did it go? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Time to open up the LRL doors, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We got you coming home. It's well stocked.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay, Burn status: DELTA-TIG was zero, burn time was 2 plus 30. PAD angles: DELTA VGX after trim was 0.1, VGY 0.9, VGZ 0.1. DELTA-VC minus 17.9, fuel 10.6, OX 10.4, unbalance minus 50.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy, Neil. Sounds good to us.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And Apollo 11, Houston. All your systems look real good to us. We'll keep you posted.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Hey, Charlie boy, looking good here. That was a beautiful burn. They don't come any finer.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. I wondered if you've compared your state vector accuracy with the one in the LM flights? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and it looked very nice. VERB 83 was plus 00070 and minus 00008.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. I was looking at your bank Bravo nitrogen tank. It didn't leak a bit - correction - didn't leak a bit this time. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Looked good here.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Chamber pressure was hanging in there around 100. The latter part, of the burn it started oscillating a little bit and got down a little bit below 100.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: 96 or so.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Would you give us P00 in ACCEPT? We've got a REFSMMAT for you. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We've got the load in. You can go back to BLOCK. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We're there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Your command module film seems to be working out pretty well, Charlie, the amount we carried. Looks like we carried just about what we needed.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Wonderful.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We have one 16 millimeter roll on the ASA 1000 color interior film. We were thinking of shooting that during the entry, out window number 4 on a bracket, and you might get the camera guide sometime in the next couple of days and give us all the good settings for that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. I wondered if during the TEI burn you utilized the oxidizer flow valve on the PUGS. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Based on your very excellent briefing I was expecting the thing to continue desiring increase for the whole time, so we started out with it in INCREASE. I saw that we pretty quickly crossed the line and started falling about 6 or 7 percent behind, so I was still expecting it to move up, and then I went down to FULL DECREASE and brought it back down to a difference of 2 percent. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you very much, Buzz.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Two tenths of a percent, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You can go to PTC attitude and torque at your - and do the P52 and torque at your convenience. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Hey, we got to take some more pictures, Charlie. Is there any constraint, normally, in staying here for awhile?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: How does that tracking look, or is it too early to tell?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by, Mike.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. FIDO's are looking at the data. It's too early to tell yet exactly. It's looking real good so far. We'll have you some answers shortly on trajectory. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. What FIDO is that?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's Jay Green.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Howdy, Jay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We have a DAP CSM update for you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. CSM weight, Mike: 26370. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Welcome.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We've taken your onboard vector and propagated it forward, and it's looking real good. We only got about 24 minutes of tracking now. Really too early to tell on the radar. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Mike, did you notice any transients at ignition on TEI? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. The transients were more noticeable than on the previous burns, Charlie. I just wrote it off on the fact we had a light command module, but there was considerable roll activity which dampened down after the first 20 seconds, I would guess, of the burn; but then there was also some pitch and yaw activity. I don't believe it was abnormal, and it seemed to be deadbanding ratherly crisply in roll plus or minus about 8 degrees either side of the center line; and after the first couple of - oh, after the first 20 seconds or so, the gimbals were quiet, and pitch and yaw were relatively quiet. Before that, there was some oscillation but mostly just in rates. Total attitude hung in there pretty well.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you much. We were looking at the playback, and we saw some things that - right at start up. We'll be back with you later on that.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Have you finished taking pictures? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We're just finishing up, Charlie.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: About to get started on the P52 here pretty soon.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Copy.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Another eight or nine of them.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. You can crank up on the PTC at any time. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: All right-o.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. This is the regional CAP COMM. Congratulations on an outstanding job. You guys have really put on a great show up there. I think it's about time you powered down and got a little rest, however. You've had a mighty long day here. Hope you're all going to get a good sleep on the way back. I look forward to seeing you when you get back here. Don't fraternize with any of those bugs in route except for the Hornet.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, boss. We'll - We're looking forward to a little rest and a restful trip back. And see you when we get there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You've earned it.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. We'd like you to turn off O2 tank number 1 heaters. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It's off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. For your information, the LGC in Eagle just went belly up at 7 hours. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Very good, ... death of a real winner, there.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Charlie, we're going to rotate about pitch 270 degrees on the way home vice 1 - or 090 on the way out. Right?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Right, sir.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. VERB 49 maneuver to that attitude is in progress.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, crew status report. Radiation: CDR 11017, CMP 10019,LMP 09020. No medication.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again, please, Neil. We - you were breaking up. We missed that. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. This is crew status report. Radiation: CDR 11017, CMP 10019, LMP 09020. No medication.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: And we didn't get any crew status report from you this morning. Wondered if you could give us an estimate of sleep last night. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay ...

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. We'll take a guess, Charlie, and try to give an equivalent amount. Oh, it's CDR 3, and LMP 4.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And, Charlie, you want the fans cycled ... Right?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative, and we'd like you to disable quads Charlie and Delta. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Charlie and Delta.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. If it's convenient, we'd like to go through your onboard readout. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Oh, excuse me. It's on the flight plan, 3102. We'd like BATTS and RCS. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Ready to copy, Houston?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: BATT Charlie 370, PYRO BATT A 370, BATT B 370; RCS, 55, 65, 64, and 62. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy all that. Thank you much.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. A couple of questions for the Moon walkers, if you got a second. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Neil. We're seeing some temperature rises on the passive seismic experiment that are a little higher than normal and were wondering if you could verify the deployed position. We understand it's about 40 feet from the LM in the eleven o'clock position. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: No. It's about in the nine or nine thirty position, and I'd say it's about 50 or 60 feet.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Copy. Also, did you notice - was there any indication of any dust cloud as you lifted off? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Not very much. There was quite a bit of Kapton and parts of the LM that went out in all directions, usually for great distances, as far as I can tell. But I don't remember seeing anything of a dust cloud to speak of.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Understand all you could see was parts of the LM going out. What was your - your first - first comment? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I don't remember. Just that the Kapton and other parts on the LM staging scattering all around the area for great distances, but I didn't see much dust.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Could you keep me honest on the lithium hydroxide changes? When do you have the next one scheduled for?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Mike, on that canister, we had you due to change one at 133 before TEI, and it's on page 399. The next one we got is at 147. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11, Houston. We'd like to extend our damping period for another 5 minutes; let the rates get way down. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: 11. Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger, Charlie. Like to bring you up to date on our chlorination status. In compartment B4, we have one, two, three, four, five, six, seven - correction, we have eight pockets for chlorine and buffer ampules, of which - Let me correct that. We have seven pockets, of which one is empty and always has been empty, leaving six remaining. On the other side over there in B7, we have another container with seven pockets, so we have a total of seven plus six, and those are filled with six chlorines and seven buffers. Now, I've been using one chlorine and one buffer per day which, at this point in time, prior to this chlorination I'm about to do, leaves me one chlorine and two buffers. Seems to me I'm one chlorine short, and that being the case, I'd like to ask your advice on postponing this chlorination using the last container until some later date, like maybe tomorrow. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy, Mike. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. Check in A1, Mike, and see what you can find in there. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We think you might have some more chlorine up in A1. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Do you read? You're breaking up. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Read.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. You're breaking up. Mike, please look in compartment A1. We think there might be some more chlorine up there. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Eureka!

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Reading you about one by. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We're having a downlink problem. That's the reason we can't read you. We're switching sites. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11. Houston. How do you read now? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You're five by now, too, Mike. Thank you much. Did you copy that about A1 on that chlorine?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Eureka!

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: How about that, sports fans!

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're having a little trouble getting the yaw rate damped out to the appropriate value. We'd like you all to be quite like mice for a couple of minutes and let's see if that will help it out. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. You did great work there. We're ready to spin it up. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Did you copy? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes. We read you, Charlie. Would you stand by a minute?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. No hurry.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. Shift change time, here. White Team bids you good night; we'll see you tomorrow. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Good night, Charlie. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Good night, Charlie. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Adios.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Adios. Thanks again for a great show, you guys.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thanks for a great job down there.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Ron.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Howdy there, Mike. We're ready to go ahead and have you switch to your OMNI positions for your sleep period, and we would like the following high gain switch positions: your high gain antenna in MANUAL, beam width WIDE, pitch is minus 50, and yaw is a plus 270. And just follow the flight plan for remaining COMM configuration. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You "Purple" people keep funny hours.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Your COMM is pretty weak at this point, Mike. Please say again.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Disregard.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It's on the way now.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We'd like for you to go ahead and put your S band antenna OMNI to OMNI and OMNI B. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. How do you read me through Honeysuckle now? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: You're loud and clear. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Very good. Reading you better now. And did you copy we'd appreciate going S band OMNI and OMNI B at this time? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's the configuration we're in.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: I'll say you "Purple" people keep funny hours.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Houston. Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Good morning, 11. This is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Crew status report: 88 and 8.5.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. 88 and 8.5. When you're ready, we've got a small flight plan update for you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, we're ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. At about 148 hours, if you've not already done so, a CO2 filter change, and the H2 purge line heater on 20 minutes before the O2 and H2 purge. At 148 hours, we'd like you to initiate a charge on battery Alfa instead of at 151 hours, and leave the charge on until we notify you further. At 150 hours GET, waste water dump to 10 percent. We do plan to burn midcourse correction 5. It will be an RCS burn about 5 feet per second at about the nominal time in the flight plan. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Understand. We'll be accomplishing the filter change shortly, the purge line heater is on ***, O2 and H2 purge shortly, and at 148 will initiate a charge on battery A until you notify us further. At 150 hours, waste water dump to 10 percent. And we're looking forward to midcourse correction 5 at about 5 feet per second at the nominal time. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. I've got your consumables update, if you're ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. At GET of 147 plus 00, RCS total minus 2.0 percent, which is about minus 14 pounds. Alfa minus 12.0, Bravo plus 10.0, minus 3.0, minus 2.0. Hydrogen total minus 1.5 pounds, O2 total plus 20 pounds. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I copy, and our onboard readouts: Alfa, *** 2 percent, Bravo 54 percent, Cocoa's 64 percent, Delta 61 percent. Over. *** Three asterisks denote clipping of words and phrases.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. Would you read that quad Alfa again, please, Buzz. You're cutting out. It may be - are you operating on VOX? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Negative. Alfa is 53 percent. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, from down here on telemetry, all your systems look to be in good shape.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Would you ask Buzz to check his biomedical TM sensors for a loose or dried out sensor? We're getting an erratic electrocardiogram reading. That would be one of the three sternal leads. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Say again your last, please.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Disregard.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Stand by for a Mark leaving the lunar sphere of influence.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: MARK.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: You're leaving the lunar sphere of influence. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Is Bill Shaffer down there?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Negative. But we've got a highly qualified team on in his stead.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. I wanted to hear him explain it again to the press conference.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That's old Apollo 8 junk, but tell him the spacecraft gave a little jump as it went through the ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll pass it on to him. Thanks a lot, and Dave Reed is sort of burying his head in his arms right now.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Those guys down there in the press room did a pretty good job this morning.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes, they have.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We don't want them to give up yet, though.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: No. They'll hang in there for about another 47 hours or so.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. If you're not busy now, I can read you up the morning news.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. We're all listening.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again, 11?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. We're all listening. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. From the hot wires of the Public Affairs Office: Apollo 11 still dominates the news around the world. Only four nations, Communist China, North Korea, North Viet Nam, and Albania, have not yet informed their citizens of your flight and landing on the Moon. One newsman said that he has run out of ways to describe your success. Tonight, President Nixon is scheduled to watch the All Star baseball game in Washington. After the game, he will depart for the Pacific recovery area. Wednesday evening, he will fly from Johnston Island by helicopter to the Navy communications ship Arlington. Then on Thursday morning, he will reboard the helicopter and fly to the Hornet in time to witness your splashdown. Accompanying the President will be Secretary of State William Rogers and Frank Borman. They will watch the splashdown from the bridge of the recovery ship with Admiral John Sidney McCain, Jr., Commander of the Pacific Forces. Following the President's stay aboard the Hornet, he will depart for his tour of Asia and scheduled visit to Romania. Luna 15 is believed to have crashed into the Sea of Crises yesterday after orbiting the Moon 52 times. The Soviet News Agency TASS reported that "scientific" "research in near Moon space was carried out." Sir Bernard Lovell at Jodrell Bank Observatory said that Luna 15 hit the surface of the Moon at a speed of about 300 miles per hour. Things have been relatively quiet recently in Viet Nam. GI's on patrol were observed carrying transistor radios tuned into your flight. The Armed Forces radio and TV network in Viet Nam gave the mission full coverage. Skirmishes still continue between the Egyptians and Israelis along the Suez Canal. U.N. observers there are trying to halt the action. In Washington, the House Ways and Means Committee has voted to reduce the 27.5 percent oil depletion allowance to 20 percent. We've had rain several times here in the Houston area. Today it is cloudy, and more showers are expected. On the sports front, as we mentioned earlier, the All Star game is tonight. There were no games played yesterday. Last night in New York, the Baseball Writers Association of America named Babe Ruth the greatest ball player of all time. Joe DiMaggio was named the greatest living ball player. Frank Borman made the announcements at a dinner honoring the players. Joe Namath put in a full day at the New York Jets' training camp. Five policemen had a hard time restraining about 500 kids who wanted to touch Broadway Joe. He said he feels fine and will play in the All Star game August 1, if Coach Weeb Eubank lets him. The Oilers' camp at Kerrville got wet yesterday, but the workouts continued. There have been some minor injuries, but nothing too serious. Coach Wally Lemm is satisfied so far with the workouts. The Oilers are expecting attendance by over 30.000 for the preseason game with Buffalo. Apparently, Don Meredith's announced retirement isn't expected to dampen enthusiasm, especially around here in Houston. Mario Andretti won the 200 mile Trenton Auto Race Sunday and is now the leading race driver in the U.S. Auto Club's point standings. And that's about the summary of the morning news this afternoon in Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Look up the Dow Jones Industrials for us.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We see you in P00. When you can give us ACCEPT, we have a state vector and target load uplink ready for you.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger, Houston. I'm going ahead and start the computer.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, we've completed the uplink. The computer's yours.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. With respect to the Dow Jones industrials, since closing on Tuesday afternoon the 15th up to about 1:05 p.m. Houston time this afternoon, why, the effect has been a net drop; that is, minus 6 points on the industrial average. So far today since opening, the Dow Jones industrial average has gone down by 11.05 after rising 1 1/2 shortly after opening. Today's performance on the utilities is a drop of 1.63, and railroads a drop of 1.58. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Every flight has to have some disadvantages, I guess.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. There is some speculation that you all are responsible for that 1 1/2 point rise right after opening.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Well, don't blame the 11 point drop on us, anyway.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. If you have a minute or so free, I wonder if we could get Mike to give us a little bit of clarification on what happened around about the time of docking. We copied him as mentioning that contact was very smooth, almost imperceptible; and we're a little bit inquisitive or curious about his remarks as to what happened after probe retraction. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. I docked in CMC AUTO, and as I said, I wasn't really sure of the moment of contact. I kept cross checking the docking probe indicators. I got two barber poles indicating that the three capture latches - not capture latches, but the three ... latches had made, and we were soft docked. And at that time the situation looked very stable. So, I went to CMC FREE, glanced back out the window and it still looked stable; and I fired primary 2 bottle. And at that time, a gyration began between the two vehicles due I'm not sure to what. Perhaps the LM thrusting or perhaps it was building up prior, and I hadn't noticed it. But anyway, during the RETRACT of the probe, there were yaw - my yaw excursions of, I would guess, around 15 degrees, and I had to come back on, take the FREE switch and throw it back to AUTO, and try to damp them out; and I guess Neil was doing the same in the LM. I'll let him tell you about his side of it. And I though that we were not going to get a successful RETRACT and hard dock. However, in about - oh, I guess 6 or 8 seconds, I did hear - could see the situation damping out, and then we heard the noise indicating the docking latches had fired; and later on when I got into the tunnel, all 12 of them had properly engaged.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And on the LM side, we were in AGS MIN deadband ATT HOLD; and at contact, I thrusted plus X; and shortly after that we had a sizable attitude oscillation and thruster firing, so we opened up the deadband to MAX and manually flew the vehicle into stable attitude during the retraction. It went to OFF after ...

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Thank you very much. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. I have your midcourse correction 5 PAD available when you're ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Ready to copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. Midcourse correction number 5, RCS/G&N: 26025, pitch and yaw trim NA, TIG 150 29 5453, minus 00048, plus all balls, plus 00001 075 159 328; HA is NA; HP plus 00230 00048 011 00048; sextant star 03 0908 382. Boresite star block, none available. Latitude plus 1102, minus 17204 11803 36275 195 03 33, GDC align, Deneb and Vega, 007 144 068, no ullage, of course, four quad thrusting. Over. Readback.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Midcourse number 5, RCS/G&N: 26025, pitch and yaw NA, 150 29 5453, minus 00048, plus all zeros, plus 00001 075 159 328, NA, plus 00230 00048 011 00048 03 0908 382, NA three times, plus 1102, minus 17204 11803 36275 195 03 33, Deneb and Vega, 007 144 068, and four quads for the burn. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Readback correct. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. If Neil has a free minute, we've got a question or two regarding the CO2 partial pressure and water in the suit loop discrepancies noted yesterday. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. Was water noted in both suits or only in yours, Neil?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I think only in my suit.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you locate that occurrence for us in time when you first noticed water in the suit, either by mission time or relation to any particular event?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I think it was after insertion sometime, Bruce. I don't remember exactly when. I - It was when we were in orbit and had our - after we took our helmets off.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Did you call it to us when you first noticed it, or was it sometime after when you called it?

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: I'd guess it might have been probably 20 minutes after I noticed it that I mentioned it to you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Was this noticing the water accompanied by erratic CO2 partial pressure readings, or was that a separate problem? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Well, the water problem evidenced itself before we noted any erratic motions of the PC02 gage.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And what was the relative sequence on selecting water separator number 2 and the secondary CO2 canister; that is, did you go to the secondary water separator first and then the secondary CO2? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I believe we went to secondary CO2 first.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Secondary hydroxide - lithium hydroxide.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy. And was there any change in your suit loop - -

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: I should mention, Bruce, that when I went to water secondary - water separator to secondary there, I didn't notice any change. But about after 15 minutes or 20 minutes, the water stopped coming out. So maybe that was just water that was already in the loop that was still blowing out, but the secondary water separator was operating properly.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Did you make any changes in the suit loop configuration after you went from the egress mode to the cabin mode after insertion; that is, in particular, they're interested in knowing if you recall changing the diverter valve position to EGRESS at any time while you were on the secondary canister? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: No. I don't believe we did that at all, Bruce.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay, 11. Thank you. That sums up our questions for now, and we'll crank these back into the engineering pipeline and see what we can come up with.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Okay. Are you satisfied that the CO2 circuit breaker was in on jettison? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again, please?

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. On LM jettison, are you satisfied that the CO2 circuit breaker was in? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Yes. It was in.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Could you confirm that? I thought there was some question after we got into the command module as to whether that had been left in or not. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11. It was in and confirmed in, and the readings after jettison stayed about 0.1 to 0.2.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We have not noticed any change in the signal coming through on the LMP's EKG. When he has a little free time, we'd like him to check into it again. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I looked at all three of the upper chest center ones, and they appear to be fairly tight. I'll push them back in again. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. On the TM here, we noticed some fluctuations that may have been attributed to your moving the sensors around or pushing on them, but the erratic problem seems to be persisting.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. I wonder if you've noticed any change in the BIOMED returns you're getting. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Negative, Buzz. It still looks kind of bad. Apparently, when you move around, it's cutting in and out. Have you checked the little electrical connector where it goes into the signal conditioner? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Yes. They're all about as tight as can be. I tell you what; I'll take them off and put them back on again and see if that makes any difference.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. If you would, at your convience, we'll be watching it down here.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We'd like you to try acquisition on the high gain antenna for us at pitch minus 90, yaw 270. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. That's in work.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, this is Houston. We're showing about 6.8 percent on waste water on our telemetry now. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. We've got about 9, up here. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We're standing by for your burn. Everything's looking good from down here.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Bruce. You've got about a minute and 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We concur.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, do you copy our residuals?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We've got your residual fuel counter reading for us.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: DELTA-VC is plus 0.2.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Plus 0.2.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: That was actually plus 100.2. Okay?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. We're in PTC attitude and would you please give us a call when our thruster activity has subsided sufficiently?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We're going to hand over from Madrid to Goldstone at 151 hours even. If you should lose lock on the high gain at this time, you may reaequire at pitch minus 45, yaw 270. Break. We're still watching your rates. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: This is 11, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, we're still seeing rates on your spacecraft above those we would like for the continuation of the PTC mode which we are still monitoring, and we'll advise you when it has settled down. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. You are go for the spinup on PTC. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Roger. It didn't like it that time. When I got down to the entry 27303 ENTER, it took off in roll at a high rate in excess of 1 degree per second. Over. I've stopped it now, and we are going to have to go back and do it over again. I'd like to try to find out the reason it did that.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You might as well start setting up for it, and we will be working the problem here.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have us on high bit rate here now?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay, good. I'll maneuver back to PTC initiation attitude while you guys look at the data and see what you think.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. I think the reason is in having 1620 on the DSKY during the subsequent entries, or at least that's one possibility.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll check it out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. While you're waiting for the CSM to settle down and for us to look at the tapes on your latest maneuver, would you feel like answering some more questions with relation to the lunar surface? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. For 64 thousand dollars, we're still trying to work out the location of your landing site, Tranquility Base. We think it is located on LAM 2 chart at Juliet 0.5 and 7.8. Do you still have those charts on board? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Yes. Stand by one. They're packed.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. You may not have to unpack it. The position which I just gave you is slightly west of West Crater. I guess it's about two tenths of a kilometer west of it, and we were wondering if Neil or Buzz had observed any additional landmarks during descent, lunar stay, or ascent which would confirm or disprove this. One thing that we're wondering about is that if you were at this position, you would have seen the Cat's Paw during ascent just up to the north of your track. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We were looking for the Cat's Paw, too, thinking we were probably downrange, beyond the Big V. But I think that it's likely that that might have been West Crater that we went across in landing, but - Stand by.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: We're hoping, Bruce, that our 16 mm film was working at that point in descent, and we'll be able to confirm our touchdown position. We thought that during ascent we might be able to pick up some recognizable objects close to the landing site, and we did see a number of small craters, and crater rows, and things like that, which we may be able to pick out after the fact, but we haven't been able to yet.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And the next question from our panel is for Buzz. We recall that he reported seeing a laser upon AOS of the Earth the first time after - the first REV after ascent, and we're wondering what color the beam was and if he could determine at the approximate location with respect to the Earth. Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: It was mostly white, perhaps a tinge of yellowish color to it; and it seemed to be - as I recall it, the terminator of the Earth was toward the horizon and seemed to be about a quarter to a third of the way down from - down towards the terminator of the Earth - from the opposite horizon. That's a third to a quarter Earth radii. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And that puts it in the light side? Over.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: Roger. Yes, it was in the light side. The Earth was about - a two thirds lit Earth, with the terminator down toward the horizon. And now coming from the opposite limb of the Earth, the sunlight limb, coming down about one quarter to one third of a radius in from the limb. Generally, pensively located with respect to a line drawn perpendicular to the terminator that goes through the center. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, Buzz. We copy.

utterances.speaker: LMP
utterances.text: And I got pictures of that. I'm sure that will show up.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: And I saw that, too. It was a very bright spot of light and I confirm Buzz's observation of its position.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay, 11. Very good. Now, with respect to the documented sample container: on television it appeared to us as though the samples for that container were in fact being given - being selected in accordance with some thought or consideration being given to the rocks themselves. And we were wondering if you could give any further details from memory about any of these samples, and the context of the material or the surface from which they were taken. Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Yes. You remember I initially started on the cut side of the LM that the TV camera was on, and I took a number of samples of rocks on the surface, and several that were just subsurface - about 20 - 15 to 20 feet north of the LM. And then I recalled that that area had been probably swept pretty well by the exhaust of the descent engine, so I crossed over to the southern side of the LM, and took a number of samples from the area around the elongate double crater that we commented on, and several beyond that, and tried to take as many different types - of rock types as I could see by eye - as I could in the short time we had available. There were a number of other samples that I had seen earlier in our stroll around the LM that I had hoped to get back and pick up and put in the documented sample, but I didn't get those, and I'll be able to comment in detail when we get in the debriefing session.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Did you observe any small craters with conspicuously blocky rims? Over.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Well, aside from the one big one that we went over, I guess there were none in our area. I took a stroll back after putting up the EASEP, and while Buzz was starting to unpack the documented samples - took a stroll back to a crater behind us that was maybe 70 or 80 feet in diameter and 15 or 20 feet deep, and took some pictures of it. It had rocks in the bottom of pretty good size, considerably bigger than any that were out on the surface, but there was no - we apparently, at 15 feet or so, had not gotten below the regolith. We were essentially showing no bedrock, at least in the walls of the crater at that depth. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy,

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Neil. That about wraps up the questions we have on hand for now.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: My compliments to the chef. The food is outstanding. This cream of chicken soup I give at least three spoons.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. Cream of chicken, three spoons.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, we concur that having VERB 16, NOUN 20 up on the DSKY may well have had some effect on your PTC initiation. It looks like this would give - let the computer work with a knowledge of the actual CDU angles. What we'd like you to do is do a CDU zero which is VERB 40, NOUN 20, ENTER, and then start the PTC procedure again at step 2 with loading VERB 6, NOUN 22, desired attitude in the AUTO maneuver, and all that. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. The only thing I don't understand about that is why it took off at the rate it did. What rate should it have taken off at under that theory?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Stand by a minute, Mike.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, CMP, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Mike, over here on page 9 7 of your checklist where we're setting up PTC, there's been a note penciled in after, "Wait 20 minutes for rate to damp. Do not monitor VERB 16, NOUN 20." It turns out that the significance of that is that, if you are monitoring 16 NOUN 20, then when you get down here in step 7, the second time you do a VERB 24, you've got to reload the NOUN 01 to make it VERB 24, NOUN 01, ENTER, before you load the three registers. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger, that. I was just questioning the rate at which the maneuver would begin if that were not done.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We're still working on computing the rate for you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. We'd like you to select REACQ mode on the high gain antenna. Looks like we're about to lose you. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11, this is Houston broadcasting in the blind. If you read us, attempt to acquire on OMNI antennas. Attempt to acquire us on OMNI antennas, if you read. This is Houston. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11, this is Houston broadcasting in the blind. If you read, attempt acquisition on an OMNI antenna. Attempt acquisition using an OMNI antenna. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11, this is Houston broadcasting in the blind. If you read, attempt contact using OMNI antenna, using an 0MNI antenna. This is Houston. Out.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11, this is Houston broadcasting in the blind. If you read us, attempt acquisition using an OMNI antenna. Attempt acquisition using an OMNI antenna. This is Houston. Out.

utterances.speaker: CT
utterances.text: ... Goldstone.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11, this is Houston. Radio check. Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Loud and clear, Bruce. How me?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. What antenna are you using?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11 is calling you on the high gain. How do you read? Over.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Loud and clear on the high gain.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: So what's new?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Oh, we were wondering what was new with you up there.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: It's all very quiet. We're just sitting here letting the thruster firing damp down. When they get good enough, let us know, and we'll start this PTC.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Nice to sit here and watch the Earth getting larger and larger and the Moon smaller and smaller.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We'll give you a call when your rates have damped down sufficiently, and we're unable at the present time to predict what rate you should have seen at your last attempt to initiate PTC. We saw about 2 1/2 degrees per second. 0ver.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Buzz thinks we should have a PTC program built in the computer. He could very well be right.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Go ahead, 11.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. I was just checking the radios, and how is the thruster activity coming?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. The radios are still in good shape, and we are still waiting for your rates to decay. We've got 0.03 degrees per second in pitch now.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. We're - we're in no rush. This is a very pleasant attitude, as a matter of fact. The Sun is down in the LEB, so it's not shining through the windows and heating the place up. We've got the Earth steady out window 1. We have the Moon steadily out window 3 and, of course, we are locked up on the high gain. So as long as the thermal people are happy, we're happy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. We copy.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, this is Houston. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Go ahead, Houston.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay, 11. We are about ready to start PTC. I would like to give you some high gain antenna angles, though. We'd like to operate in the REACQ mode, and do you plan on spinning up in the positive or negative direction? 0ver.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: We can do it either way. I had planned the positive.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Okay. For positive, the high gain antenna setting should be pitch plus 30, yaw 270, and in REACQ. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Understand. REACQ, pitch plus 30, yaw 270. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. And if you would, when you're making your DSKY entries to set up for PTC, go a little slower, and we'll try to follow each entry from down here. Over.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, 11. PTC established.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger, 11.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: 11, Houston. We observe the PTC to be fairly well established here, and we'll keep you posted on how it's going, and your friendly White Team commentator is taking over now.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks to all you Black Team.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: That was the Green Team.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Correction, all you Green Team - correction, Green Team. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Roger. Out.

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: How could I forget. I used to be a "Green" one.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Hello, Apollo 11, Houston. Your White Team is now on. We're standing by for an exciting evening of TV and a presleep report. Over.

utterances.speaker: SC
utterances.text: (Laughter)

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You sure you don't have anybody else in there with you?

utterances.speaker: CMP
utterances.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Say again, please.

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: We had some strange noises coming down on the downlink, and it sounded like you had some friends up there.

utterances.speaker: CDR
utterances.text: Where - where do the White Team go during their off hours anyway?

utterances.speaker: CC
utterances.text: Say again.
